current.text: He re-signed with the Knicks for 2 years and 9 million USD.
He is a projected starter next to Brunson, Bridges, Anunoby and Towns.
He played through hand injuries last season.
The Knicks won the championship and beat the Spurs in the Finals.
Experts expect his minutes to stay around 30 per game. They see no return to 36 to 38 minute roles because the Knicks will be careful with workloads.
The Knicks are expected to be conservative early, with starters' minutes trimmed and more rest on back-to-backs.
Experts worry about a championship hangover for the Knicks: a minute or two less per game and a small rise in injury risk.
He is called the Knicks starter most at risk of decline because of past wear and tear, and he showed signs of decline last season.
Experts see him as overpriced. In an auction mock the expert would pay no more than 2 USD for him (he went for 8 USD), and his ESPN and points-league draft spots are called too high.
His block rate fell last season and could move back up.
The Knicks are projected to win about 50 to 54 games.

durable.text: He is a fantasy stat stuffer whose game relies on motor and athleticism.
He is historically a 31 to 33 percent three-point shooter.
Rebounds are his strongest category, clearly above other guards and forwards. Assists and steals are also above the pool. No category is a real outlier either way.

note: Hart ranks about 97 to 98 on both sites, with values of 4 USD (Yahoo) and 3 USD (ESPN). He sold for 6 USD in our league last season, and experts would pay no more than about 2 USD. He fits any build as a late filler for rebounds, assists and steals (REB z +1.9 vs his position), but his minutes are expected to stay near 30. Pay 1 to 3 USD at most, and check early whether the Knicks hold him under 30 minutes and rest him on back-to-backs over the first 30 or so games.
